text:
Maria: Quick follow-up from the fidelity-budget RFC — we still need to lock the manifest fields and the runtime handshake for reporting quality. Can we decide today?

Devon: Prefer to avoid extra RPCs per request. Proposal: request can include `profile_request` header and runtime returns `quality_hint` in response metadata. Telemetry emits per-request degscore histograms.

Priya: That sounds ok. Two questions — how do tenant overrides work and who can opt in? Allowlist or global opt-out? @Devon?

Devon: I lean allowlist (explicit opt-in) so we don't regress noisy customers. We also need a default safe profile for everyone.

Noah: If allowlist, runtime should fall back to `fallback_profile` defined in manifest when no allowed override exists. Also: per-shard calibration blobs need version tags so we can roll back.

quantops-bot: canary deployed to staging-dedicated-2 with shadow sampling=10% for the new profile handshake :rocket:

Anya: We should bake a calibration step into the profile lifecycle. Save per-shard calibration vector to KV and reference it from manifest via `calibration_version`. Example manifest snippet:```yaml
profiles:
  - id: fp8-lite
    fallback_profile: int8-safe
    calibration_version: v1.2
    quality_budget: "0.985"
    allowed_overrides: ["tenant-alpha", "tenant-beta"]
```

Devon: How do we measure `quality_budget`? Operationally it's a threshold on eval degscore. My suggestion: define it as the 95th-percentile loss of our canned eval set (i.e., 95% of eval prompts must be >= budget).

Iris: Observability note: per-token tracing is expensive. Telemetry sampling must be adjustable per-tenant (default 1%), and increase to 100% only in short canaries. We should expose `telemetry.sample_rate` in the manifest.

Priya: Ops play — if runtime detects `calibration_version` mismatch at load, it should auto-fallback to `fallback_profile` and emit an alert to #eng-oncall. I'll add a short runbook. Link to draft: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quant-calib-fallback (draft).

Maria: Actionable next step: I'll update the RFC with an explicit handshake: on model-load the runtime advertises `supported_profiles` + `calibration_version`. Each request may include `profile_request`; runtime will deterministically pick profile by: (1) if tenant in `allowed_overrides` use requested profile, (2) else use `fallback_profile`, (3) if requested profile incompatible, pick highest-priority safe profile. We'll also add a `quality_hint` number in the response metadata.

Noah: Also add migration policy: staged rollout over 2 weeks with shadowing -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% and an automated regression gate: top-level metric regression < 0.5% (or rollback).

Devon: I'll implement the runtime bits and unit/integration harness for staging. Will add tests for calibration_version mismatch and sampling changes.

Maria: Great. I'll push the RFC update and open the manifest schema PR. If anyone wants to carve ownership of the sampling/telemetry pieces ping me. :thumbsup:
